Prime Number Checker

Deterministic Miller-Rabin primality test for big integers.

–
Verdict
–
Smallest factor

Deterministic Miller-Rabin for n < 2^64. Trial division searches factors up to 1,000,000.

📖 How to use

  1. Enter a positive integer (up to 2^64).
  2. Press Check.
  3. Read the prime/composite verdict.
  4. For composites, see the smallest factor if one exists below 1,000,000.

❓ Frequently asked questions

What test is used?

A deterministic Miller-Rabin test with the known-good bases 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, which is exact for every integer below 2^64 — no probability involved.

How big can the number be?

Big integers are handled natively with BigInt, exact up to 2^64. Larger inputs are rejected rather than tested imprecisely.

How is the smallest factor found?

By trial division with a prime sieve up to 1,000,000. If no factor is found in that range, the tool says so honestly instead of guessing.
